title: 3.1.8 Lab: Concessions Stand
description: Write a parameterless function, concessions(), that prints the food and drink options at a cinema, then call it. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Define concessions
steps.instructions: Define a function called concessions that takes no parameters.

steps.title: Print the options
steps.instructions: Inside the function, log exactly: Food/Drink Options: Popcorn: $8-10 Candy: $3-5 Soft drink: $5-7

steps.title: Call it
steps.instructions: Call concessions() after the definition so the body runs.

requirements.title: concessions defined, no parameters
requirements.description: Code defines a function named concessions with an empty parameter list. Help: 3.1.2 (Defining & Calling a Function)
requirements.hint: Write function concessions() { ... } with that exact name and nothing between the parentheses.

requirements.title: prints the options line
requirements.description: The function body logs the food/drink options. Help: 3.1.2 (Defining & Calling a Function)
requirements.hint: Inside the function, one console.log should list Popcorn, Candy and Soft drink in that order.

requirements.title: concessions is called
requirements.description: Code calls concessions() as a statement. Help: 3.1.2 (Defining & Calling a Function)
requirements.hint: Defining is not running. Below the function, write concessions(); to call it.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "3.1.8 Lab: Concessions Stand". The task they were given: Define a function called concessions that takes no parameters. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
